`readagau` provides reproducible access to versioned Australian agricultural
data published by the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics
and Sciences (ABARES). It discovers exact releases, caches source assets,
parses workbooks and reports into semantic observations, and retains source
identity and content-hash provenance.

The installed, package-owned synthetic fixtures make this first parser
workflow deterministic and fully offline. They are clearly marked as
documentation structures; use the package's live or reviewed local-source
paths when you need official ABARES observations.

## Install and load

Install the development version from GitHub while the package is not yet on
CRAN:

```r
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("chartwell-macro/readagau")
```

Then load the package:

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE
)

library(readagau)

fixture <- function(...) {
  path <- system.file("fixtures", ..., package = "readagau")
  stopifnot(nzchar(path))
  path
}

cache_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0("readagau-start-", Sys.getpid()))
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## First success: read a local Crop Report workbook

The package accepts a local workbook path as a release. Naming the path
`national` supplies the asset role explicitly. `view = "canonical"` asks the
package to apply its versioned precedence policy; use `view = "reported"` for
an audit of every admitted source row.

```{r first-success}
crop_path <- fixture("workbooks", "crop-national.xlsx")

crop <- read_crop_report(
  c(national = crop_path),
  assets = "national",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
validation <- validate_agau_release(crop)
stopifnot(
  inherits(crop, "crop_report_data"),
  "agau_data" %in% class(crop),
  isTRUE(validation$valid)
)

data.frame(
  class = class(crop)[1L],
  observations = nrow(crop),
  tables = length(unique(crop$table_id)),
  valid = validation$valid
)
```

The result is a tibble with product-specific class `crop_report_data` and
shared class `agau_data`. A product reader's rows include semantic dimensions
such as `table_id`, `geography`, `commodity`, `concept`, `period`, and
`period_status`, plus numeric `value`, original `raw_value`, and provenance.

```{r first-preview}
knitr::kable(utils::head(crop[c(
  "table_id", "geography", "commodity", "concept", "period",
  "period_status", "value", "unit"
)], 6L))
```

`validate_agau_release()` returns a structured
`agau_validation_report`. Its `valid` field checks required semantic fields,
controlled status and rights values, unique canonical keys, source notes, and
content-hash shape. Inspect the report when a parse fails validation instead
of silently repairing the rows.

## Checksum-qualified identity for local files

Because this file is local and no release metadata was supplied, the reader
assigns a checksum-qualified local identity. Reviewed official identity is
assigned only when the release metadata is explicit:

```{r first-identity}
local_identity <- unique(crop[c(
  "release_id", "release_date", "source_asset", "sha256", "parser_version"
)])
stopifnot(
  nrow(local_identity) == 1L,
  startsWith(local_identity$release_id, "local-"),
  is.na(local_identity$release_date),
  grepl("^[a-f0-9]{64}$", local_identity$sha256)
)
knitr::kable(local_identity)
```

For a reviewed local copy of an exact official edition, pass both
`release_id` and `release_date`; supplying only one is a validation error.
Persist those fields, the source URL, SHA-256, and `parser_version` with any
derived result.

## Discover releases and choose an exact one

`list_agau_releases()` returns release metadata and support status. With
`refresh = FALSE` and a temporary cache, this catalogue example is offline:

```{r release-catalogue}
releases <- list_agau_releases(
  products = "crop_report",
  refresh = FALSE,
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
knitr::kable(releases[seq_len(min(6L, nrow(releases))), c(
  "release_id", "release_date", "support_status", "unsupported_reason"
)])
```

Discovery metadata records support status separately. Choose a supported exact
release with an admitted asset role and parser profile for reproducible work;
`"latest"` remains available for exploration.

## Retrieve and chart a time series

Inspect the installed registry, select stable source IDs, and pass exact dated
snapshots to `read_agau_prices()`. This example uses A2 (wheat) and A3 (corn)
and retains the returned date, value, and series columns. Its installed
fixtures are package-owned synthetic structures, so the chart demonstrates
the real offline parser path rather than official prices.

```{r discover-series}
weekly_registry <- agau_series_catalog("weekly_commodity_prices")
selected_series <- c("A2", "A3")
weekly_registry[
  weekly_registry$source_series_id %in% selected_series,
  c("source_series_id", "indicator", "commodity", "market", "source_provider")
]
```

```{r retrieve-series}
weekly_fixture_names <- c(
  "weekly-2016-10-13.txt", "weekly-2018-03-08.txt",
  "weekly-2018-05-17.txt", "weekly-2018-07-05.txt",
  "weekly-2018-10-18.txt", "weekly-2019-05-16.txt",
  "weekly-2019-06-06.txt", "weekly-2021-03-25.txt",
  "weekly-2025-07-10.txt"
)
weekly_fixture_paths <- file.path(
  system.file("fixtures", "text", package = "readagau"),
  weekly_fixture_names
)

weekly_history <- read_agau_prices(
  snapshot = weekly_fixture_paths,
  series = selected_series,
  measures = "latest_price",
  include_charts = FALSE,
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

chart_data <- weekly_history[
  weekly_history$record_role == "latest_price" &
    !is.na(weekly_history$observation_date) &
    !is.na(weekly_history$value),
  c("observation_date", "value", "commodity", "unit"),
  drop = FALSE
]
chart_data <- chart_data[
  order(chart_data$observation_date, chart_data$commodity),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
```

When `ggplot2` is installed, the following code renders the retrieved values
as a simple line chart. It is conditional so the rest of the offline article
remains runnable when the optional plotting package is unavailable.

```{r series-chart, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "Line chart of synthetic weekly wheat and corn fixture values across nine observation dates."}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = observation_date, y = value,
      colour = commodity, group = commodity
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Synthetic weekly wheat and corn series",
      subtitle = "Weekly observations from package-owned fixtures",
      x = "Observation date",
      y = "Fixture value (US$/t)",
      colour = "Commodity",
      caption = "Source: readagau package-owned synthetic fixtures"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

Every parsed row also retains release identity and content-hash provenance.
For a reproducible analysis, save `release_date`, `source_asset`, `sha256`, and
`parser_version` alongside the chart data.

## Other supported source families

The same local-first pattern applies to the other readers:

```{r other-readers}
commodities <- read_agricultural_commodities(
  c(outlook = fixture("workbooks", "ac-march-outlook.xlsx")),
  datasets = "outlook",
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
productivity <- read_farm_productivity(
  fixture("workbooks", "farm-productivity.xlsx"),
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
forecast_history <- read_agau_forecast_history(
  fixture("workbooks", "historical-forecast.csv")
)

data.frame(
  reader = c("Agricultural Commodities", "Farm Productivity", "Forecast history"),
  class = c(
    class(commodities)[1L], class(productivity)[1L],
    class(forecast_history)[1L]
  ),
  observations = c(nrow(commodities), nrow(productivity), nrow(forecast_history))
)
```

Agricultural Commodities and Crop Report readers return the shared observation
contract and support reported/canonical views. Farm Productivity adds method
and financial-year semantics. The Historical Agricultural Forecast Database
has its own `agau_forecast_history` contract because it is a forecast/actual
database rather than a release observation table.

For weekly commodity prices, pass a local HTML, PDF, Word, text, or ZIP path
to `read_agau_prices(snapshot = path)`. It returns the dedicated weekly-price
schema and source-provider fields; the vintage-comparison helpers cover the
release-product families described in the comparison article.

## Network, cache, and system requirements

The local workflows above do not require network access. Online discovery,
`release = "latest"`, missing exact assets, and current weekly pages may use
the network and cache immutable bytes under the managed
`tools::R_user_dir("readagau", "cache")` location. No credentials are
required for public source pages. Prefer a dedicated temporary `cache_dir` in
examples and tests.

PDF input additionally requires the `pdftotext` executable from Poppler. HTML,
workbook, CSV, Word, and packaged-fixture workflows do not require Poppler.
Upstream layout changes are handled by schema gates: a changed or ambiguous
asset fails with a typed condition rather than being silently guessed.
